summary.en: Build a max-heap from the bottom, extract maxima and repair the shrinking heap with iterative sift-down.
summary.bn: max-heap বানিয়ে বারবার সর্বোচ্চ মান শেষে বসাও, আর build-heap-এর linear খরচ বোঝো।

notes: C17 baseline; general algorithm bounds treat input size as variable.

examples.title: Order five marks, including a tie
examples.explanationHtml: The input already forms a max-heap. Repeated root extraction produces 1 3 3 5 7.

examples.title: Sort numbers entered at the keyboard
examples.explanationHtml: The larger-child rule works for negative and positive keys alike. Extracting maxima leaves both -2 values at the front.

examples.title: Use sorted neighbours to find distinct marks
examples.explanationHtml: Heap extraction creates contiguous equal-score groups. The final scan sees three distinct scores.

examples.title: Build only the max-heap
examples.explanationHtml: Bottom-up repair produces 5 4 3 1 2. This is heap order, not ascending order; only the root maximum is immediately guaranteed.

practice.title: Find the kth largest through extraction
practice.statementHtml: Heap-sort a nonempty row and report its kth largest value, counting duplicates separately. Print Enter n, then n values:, read n (1..64) and n values (-99..99), then print Enter k: and read k (1..n). Finish with kth = V.
hints: Ascending sorted position n - k contains the kth largest record.

practice.title: Build a heap without extracting it
practice.statementHtml: Construct the bottom-up max-heap but do not perform heap-sort extraction. Display Enter n, then n values:, accept n = 0..64 and keys -99..99, then print the heap array on one space-separated line. Use the larger-child rule; keep the left child on equal-child ties.
hints: Begin at n / 2 - 1 because later positions are leaves.

practice.title: Explain the Heap Sort invariant
practice.statementHtml: For Heap Sort, state what stays true as the main process repeats. Explain the start, preservation and completed result.
hints: Use the changing boundaries and the processed region in this method.
practice.answerHtml:
Sift assumes both child subtrees are heaps. When the larger child rises, its new parent position satisfies the heap rule; only the displaced value's downward path can remain invalid. The path strictly moves towards a leaf, so repair terminates with a valid heap.

The outer extraction invariant says the prefix is a max-heap, the suffix is sorted, and no prefix value exceeds any suffix value. Moving the root to the suffix places the largest remaining value correctly. Repair restores the prefix heap without touching the suffix. Shrinking the heap to one value therefore gives a sorted permutation.

practice.title: Derive the resource cost of Heap Sort
practice.statementHtml: Use node heights for bottom-up construction and heap height for repeated root repair.
hints: Count the work from this algorithm rather than naming a class alone.
practice.answerHtml: The height of a complete binary tree is Θ(log n). Build-heap sums node heights to Θ(n), rather than charging every node the full height. Extraction costs sum to O(n log n) and the worst-case total is Θ(n log n). Iterative repair keeps auxiliary space O(1). Heap sort is not adaptive in the same useful way as insertion sort: an already ordered array does not let this version stop after a single linear verification.

quiz.prompt: For zero-based heap index r, where is its left child?
quiz.explanation: The complete-tree array representation uses 2r+1 and 2r+2.

quiz.prompt: Which child must iterative sift consider for promotion?
options: The last array value regardless of parent
quiz.explanation: The promoted parent must dominate both children.

quiz.prompt: Why does bottom-up build-heap take linear time?
options: The tree has only one level
Most nodes have very small height
quiz.explanation: Summing node heights gives a convergent weighted series times n.

quiz.prompt: After swapping root with a[end], which length is passed to sift?
quiz.explanation: The final position end must be excluded from the active heap.

quiz.prompt: Is a max-heap necessarily an ascending array?
options: No; it guarantees parent-child order only
Yes; every left value is smaller
Yes; its root is the minimum
quiz.explanation: Sibling and cross-subtree positions need not be globally ordered.

quiz.prompt: Which workspace claim fits iterative heap sort?
quiz.explanation: The array itself stores the heap and sift is iterative.

quiz.prompt: Why can heap sort reverse equal-key records?
options: Root-end exchanges can jump across equal records
It directly compares every equal pair as unequal
quiz.explanation: A distant exchange can change tie order without an equal-pair swap.

quiz.prompt: At root index 2, which left-child index is computed?
Which child is selected when child keys are 3 and 5?
quiz.explanation: The larger right child is at index 2.

quiz.prompt: For n = 5, which root begins bottom-up heap construction?
quiz.explanation: Integer division gives 2, so the last parent index is 1.

keyPoints.en: A max-heap exposes a largest value at its root.
keyPoints.bn: Max-heap-এর root-এ একটি সর্বোচ্চ মান থাকে।

keyPoints.en: Sift down chooses the larger child.
keyPoints.bn: Sift down-এ বড় child-টি বেছে নাও।
নিচ থেকে heap বানাতে linear কাজ লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Shrink the active heap after extraction.
keyPoints.bn: সর্বোচ্চ মান বের করার পর heap-এর সীমা ছোট করো।

keyPoints.en: Iterative heap sort uses constant extra storage.
keyPoints.bn: Iterative heap sort-এ constant বাড়তি জায়গা লাগে।
সাধারণ heap sort-এ সমান key-এর ক্রম নাও থাকতে পারে।

examQuestions.question: For [7,3,5,3,1], show bottom-up max-heap construction and the full array after each root extraction and repair. Mark the shrinking active heap.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
StageStateDecision
Build[7,3,5,3,1]The input already satisfies the max-heap rule.
end = 4[5,3,1,3,7]Move 7 to the suffix and repair the root.
end = 3[3,3,1,5,7]Move 5 into its final position.
end = 2[3,1,3,5,7]One 3 joins the completed suffix.
end = 1[1,3,3,5,7]Only the minimum remains active.
